desert_p16_001.speaker: narrator
desert_p16_001.text: The relay door had no inscription. Du noticed this before he noticed the wall around it, and Gao noticed his disappointment. Morning light fell across the outer court in pale rectangles broken by a collapsed roof edge. The mason had already inspected the firm approach, the remaining buttress and the standing portion of the court wall. He allowed a small party along the cleared line, with no climbing on the rubble or gathering beneath the unsupported corner. Yue carried the light flags and one support board. The conservator carried her own box.

desert_p16_002.speaker: narrator
desert_p16_002.text: Behind them the village nephew pointed out the place where gardeners sorted bulbs in the wall's long afternoon shade. On the outer wall, a swallow had built a mud cup beneath the surviving ledge. Its nest occupied precisely the corner Du wanted to use for his first drawing. The bird returned with a bead of damp material and looked at the people below as if their permission had never occurred to it. Gao shifted the drawing position to the doorway's other side. The conservator approved.

desert_p16_003.speaker: narrator
desert_p16_003.text: Her own office had once spent a morning arguing about moving a nesting bird when three shelves beneath a leak needed attention first. The swallow settled into its work. Yue wrote the shifted position on the sketch and hoped the bird would not become the room's grandest discovery. They had begun with the channel rather than the door. At first light Gao and the mason rechecked the monitored cart approach. Its reference edge had not moved since evening, and the supporting shelf remained within the assessed margin.

desert_p16_004.speaker: narrator
desert_p16_004.text: The lower spill throat, however, held a tangle of branches against one old bar. Water passed through the remaining opening faster than it had below the quarry. Gao measured the accessible levels from stable points while the nephew described last season's ordinary depth. His memory was useful background, not a graduated gauge. The present readings and obstruction gave the district officer an immediate reason to examine the receiving work. The mason's sounding rod struck different notes along the spill throat's accessible side. Solid stone gave a short blunt answer; a loosened facing rang more hollow.

desert_p16_005.speaker: narrator
desert_p16_005.text: He showed Gao the boundary without asking her to lean over it. The nephew remembered that section being repaired with smaller blocks after a flood. A repair could explain the different sound without proving it stable under the present flow. Gao marked both the condition and the old account. Yue watched the water press through the branch tangle. It carried seeds and grit in ordinary abundance, all the little things a map's blue line had never bothered to carry.

desert_p16_006.speaker: gao_ru
desert_p16_006.text: We are not going to pull the branches from above and see what happens. There is stored water on the upstream side and an occupied path below. The responsible crew needs the levels, the obstruction drawing and the downstream people identified. We can send that now. The current cart track remains as assessed this morning, but if its lower edge changes we leave it. The nephew's market wagon goes toward the quarry before noon. Let the written urgency travel with it, and give the household representatives the same account before we go near the relay.

desert_p16_007.speaker: gao_ru
desert_p16_007.text: They should not learn about their water from a copy printed in town.

desert_p16_008.speaker: narrator
desert_p16_008.text: Du suggested they could recover the old gate board's position from the inventory before the foreman answered. Gao said they might recover a description, not an operating instruction. He looked annoyed, then admitted he had wanted a page to improve the scene immediately. The mason asked him to hold the drawing board instead. Du took it. While he held it, he could see the current flowing past his shoes at a distance no paragraph changed. The practical task steadied him. He asked the nephew which lower path people used during floods and copied that answer beside the historical gate sketch.

desert_p16_009.speaker: narrator
desert_p16_009.text: Some useful things were available before the old room opened. The nephew carried the message to the well court. A resident with a market wagon agreed to deliver it directly to the named quarry foreman on his outward journey, using his own travel stock and route. Gao kept a dated duplicate and asked for the receiving answer when there was a real returning messenger. The household representatives began keeping people away from the lower crossing's splash line.

desert_p16_010.speaker: narrator
desert_p16_010.text: They did not close the currently stable footbridge merely because distant clouds existed, but placed an adult observer near its approach while garden work continued. The party's report had changed the day's work without pretending the visitors controlled every stream. The market wagon's driver wore a cap with a long bill bent upward at one corner. Yue recognized him from the reed village's receiving yard, where he had argued over a screen price and eventually paid it. He read the urgent message once, asked which foreman actually had authority, and repeated the name aloud to be sure.

desert_p16_011.speaker: narrator
desert_p16_011.text: Gao gave him the contact point. He said he would leave his ordinary goods at the quarry buyer before seeking the foreman, unless the receiving yard was on his first turn. It was. The promised delivery now fitted his route rather than floating above it as an act of vague kindness. He placed the note in his dry pouch and left. Tuo remained at the firm upper turn with a chair and the current route sheets. From there she could see the cart shoulder and the relay's outer court without walking its broken edge.

desert_p16_012.speaker: narrator
desert_p16_012.text: Bao examined the camp treatment space and stayed within easy call until the first approach was settled. The drivers kept the mules on the upper communal shoulder. Only Gao, Du, Yue, the conservator, the mason and the paid local nephew approached the cleared court, entering in the small groups the mason allowed rather than crowding one narrow patch. The old building made people feel like visitors even when the work scope said they could be there. Tuo's chair at the upper turn faced the narrow valley and a patch of shade that moved faster than she wanted.

desert_p16_013.speaker: narrator
desert_p16_013.text: Yue helped shift it along the firm standing line while Bao checked the support under her foot. Tuo complained that the room had managed to be interesting only when she could not enter it. Bao said the room had probably been interesting yesterday too, when no visitor was there to approve. Tuo threatened to hire a more flattering clinician next time. Bao offered to write that in the treatment note under impractical requests. They both smiled. Yue left the route sheets within Tuo's reach, weighted against the north wind by two plain stones.

desert_p16_014.speaker: narrator
desert_p16_014.text: The nephew called the door the Quiet Shutter. Children had been told to leave it alone because the inner room belonged to the closed office and because the wood could catch a finger. Its outer hinges were iron under old dust, not a concealed cultivation mechanism. A broken plaster patch above it showed the end of a former lintel painting. Du tried to compare the remaining strokes with the inventory's receiving niche. The conservator asked him to wait until the dust had settled from their footsteps. He stepped back so sharply that Yue nearly laughed.

desert_p16_015.speaker: narrator
desert_p16_015.text: His desire to recognize the room was stronger than his ability to stand still inside it. The nephew showed the mason an old handprint in the shutter's dust. It had been made years before by his cousin, who claimed she had nearly opened the room and discovered a dragon ledger. He had suspected she meant a ledger with a dragon on the cover. The conservator asked whether anyone had entered more recently. He knew of no entry, only gardeners using the outside shade. Gao wrote that as his local knowledge, leaving space for other accounts.

desert_p16_016.speaker: narrator
desert_p16_016.text: Du asked whether the cousin still lived in the hollow. She had married into the quarry district and could be asked. A dragon ledger, if real, was probably going to lose its dragon before the week ended. The mason examined the doorway's arch and side joints before anyone touched the shutter. The standing masonry supported this small opening independently of the collapsed outer roof section. He found no present separation at the sound inner springing, though two loose plaster pieces required removal by controlled hand work. He cleared them while the others remained back.

desert_p16_017.speaker: narrator
desert_p16_017.text: Then he tested the shutter's lower edge with a plain timber wedge, keeping force away from the brittle surrounding plaster. It shifted a little. The conservator put a sheet beneath the gap to catch loose material without letting it blow into the room. Yue steadied the sheet's outside corner at her direction. The mason let Yue brush loose grit from the wedge's working place using the small plain brush he lent her. Her healed palms tolerated the light task; she did not grip the wedge or brace the shutter.

desert_p16_018.speaker: narrator
desert_p16_018.text: When she returned the brush, its bristles had acquired one long pale thread. The conservator looked at the thread and recognized old woven screen fibre rather than a page. She bagged the sweepings only because their position would matter if the screen's failure later had to be described. Du stared at the little packet, visibly learning how much evidence could consist of things nobody would display in a polished lecture. A smell of dry reed came through the opening, then dust and a faint old tang like ink left in a hot cupboard.

desert_p16_019.speaker: narrator
desert_p16_019.text: The shutter moved another hand's width and stopped. Its lower corner had swollen against a warped threshold during some wet season and dried there. The mason eased that corner free with a smaller wedge. No one asked Yue to supply a pulse to unknown wood. The task was already within ordinary tools, and the tools gave the worker a direct feel for resistance. When the shutter finally opened far enough for the conservator to look, Du whispered an inventory term under his breath. She held up a hand without turning.

desert_p16_020.speaker: narrator
desert_p16_020.text: A beetle emerged from the loosened threshold and crossed the clean catching sheet with great determination. Yue moved the outside corner just enough to let it reach bare stone without entering the conservator's prepared box. The mason waited while it departed. He said beetles were usually better at finding an exit than people. Du asked whether it knew another door. The mason said he had not negotiated with it. The small exchange broke the tension around the shutter. When work resumed, Du was breathing normally instead of holding his whole chest still while wood decided whether to move.

desert_p16_021.speaker: narrator
desert_p16_021.text: The room could be entered without making every creak an omen. The inner room was shallow. Its remaining roof lay beneath a thick ordinary drift that had collected behind the windward wall, making the exterior look like one continuous mound. A high slit admitted light along the rear shelf. The mason assessed the visible roof support and floor before permitting entry, allowing two people at a time on the sound near strip. The covered rear corner was not cleared for standing. The conservator entered first with the mason beside her.

desert_p16_022.speaker: narrator
desert_p16_022.text: Gao and Du waited outside, and Yue kept the support board ready. The room had been hidden by the hill's accumulated debris, not by any power that needed to recognize a rightful visitor. Through the high slit, daylight touched a narrow strip of plaster on the rear wall. Small round impressions marked its lower edge. Gao thought they might be pegs used for hanging a screen; Du remembered an inventory reference to seasonal light positions. Neither tried to settle the matter from the doorway.

desert_p16_023.speaker: narrator
desert_p16_023.text: The conservator would first assess the room, and the mason would first decide what nearer wall could be examined. Yue drew the visible impressions as holes, not stars. A secret constellation would have made a better town rumour. Ordinary holes had the advantage of admitting that somebody might once have put something useful into them. On the near shelf lay wooden dividers, two small metal weights and a closed fibre box whose lid had collapsed inward. Loose paper corners protruded beneath it. The conservator looked without lifting.

desert_p16_024.speaker: narrator
desert_p16_024.text: She measured the condition with the reading-house's plain humidity strip and compared it with the sheltered air outside. The old pages would require controlled support before any movement. One metal weight bore a scale unit, another a rough household mark. Du could see them from the doorway and wanted their inscriptions copied. She let Gao make an exterior position drawing first. Every object needed somewhere to belong before a hand gave it a new place. The metal weights looked nearly equal from outside, but the conservator's position record included their different thicknesses.

desert_p16_025.speaker: narrator
desert_p16_025.text: Du identified the marked unit on the office piece as a local trade measure now obsolete. The rough household piece had no clear standard inscription. Its present similarity could not establish that it had once measured the same thing. Gao proposed weighing neither until custody and condition allowed a proper examination. The nephew said the old village accounts sometimes used a named household stone as a reference. Du wrote that down with genuine interest. A unit could be communal work before it became a clean printed mark.

desert_p16_026.speaker: du_she
desert_p16_026.text: That is the seasonal receiving shelf. The closed office used it to separate household deposits from freight stores. The metal weights should not have been together in one tray. Unless the tray was moved after the closure, which it may have been. I am sorry. I am guessing in front of something I have wanted to see for years. Record the positions first. If the writing can be read where it lies, I can help identify the units. If it cannot, you should tell me to wait until it can.

desert_p16_027.speaker: du_she
desert_p16_027.text: I have come far enough to make waiting feel unreasonable, which is precisely why I need someone else to say it.

desert_p16_028.speaker: narrator
desert_p16_028.text: Yue had been keeping two pens ready, one for literal copied text and one for comments on the modern wrapper. When Du asked where a likely missing heading belonged, she pointed to the wrapper instead of the copied line. He smiled ruefully and accepted the distinction. The conservator thanked her without pausing her condition inspection. Yue felt the small usefulness of an arrangement she had made herself. At the kiln she had often been the person following somebody's established sequence. Here she could choose where uncertainty went on a page, and that choice would travel farther than her handwriting.

desert_p16_029.speaker: narrator
desert_p16_029.text: She made the wrapper mark a little darker. The conservator did say it. She asked him to wait with enough kindness that he could obey without acting wounded. Gao drew the shelf from the permitted doorway position and measured references the mason had cleared. Yue wrote the positions on a modern sheet. The nephew identified a local household mark resembling the rough one on the second weight, then added that many families used a similar crossed-stem design. It was a lead for comparison, not an inheritance announced by a metal object. Du accepted the qualification.

desert_p16_030.speaker: narrator
desert_p16_030.text: He had learned at least one useful thing from the crooked bird in the northern glass case. From the outer court, the north wind arrived in alternating cool and warm breaths. The high opening deepened its note when the shutter stood wide, then softened when the mason tested the door angle. Gao heard the change and asked him to hold one position long enough for an observation. The sound depended on airflow through the opening and room, not a voice trapped under the drift.

desert_p16_031.speaker: narrator
desert_p16_031.text: The nephew had known the fact in practice without naming it; he had sheltered here as a child when the note meant stronger wind outside. His memory made the explanation less impressive and more complete. Yue wrote the observed door angle beside the sound, then returned to the paper. At the rear of the room, the high slit produced a stripe bright enough to hide writing rather than reveal it. Dust drifted through the light with irritating beauty. The conservator held a clean shade outside the beam, changing the glare without touching the shelf.

desert_p16_032.speaker: narrator
desert_p16_032.text: Yue could then see the fibres of one protruding page. Its corner had curled over an inked column. Nothing moved of its own accord except dust. The shutter creaked when a gust reached the court. The nephew said the slit whistled in stronger north wind. The opening had probably been built for air and sorting light, an ordinary answer to a room that otherwise held both too poorly. The copied gate line included a small mark shaped like a fork. Du initially read it as a route division.

desert_p16_033.speaker: narrator
desert_p16_033.text: The nephew recognized the local notation for a temporary closure, used on old water boards. The older letter used the fork beside a different season. Du laid the two modern copies together and compared their neighbouring words. A route division would not fit the grammar on either. He corrected his reading before it entered Gao's summary. Yue saw the nephew hesitate, perhaps expecting his local account to be thanked and ignored. Instead Du asked him to repeat the usage slowly. The man sat down on a firm stone and did.

desert_p16_034.speaker: narrator
desert_p16_034.text: The first readable line gave a season and a receiving gate code. Gao copied it exactly, leaving the missing word as a gap. Du checked the code against the retained letter. It belonged to the relay, not the lower exchange. The line's date lay several years before the storm-delayed transfer. This was an older operating record, perhaps kept as precedent. The conservator would not release the fibre box until she could support its contents and inspect the failed lid. They could record visible headings from the doorway now.

desert_p16_035.speaker: narrator
desert_p16_035.text: Yue felt the work becoming slower just as it became interesting, as though the room insisted that curiosity travel at the speed of old paper. When the older sister arrived, she brought the herb basket rather than come empty-handed to an official-looking scene. She had expected Du to ask for dates she could not remember. He asked what her grandmother had called the covered reserve, and she answered at once: the two sleeping jars. The community had once kept contributions against lean seasons, returning portions under household accounts.

desert_p16_036.speaker: narrator
desert_p16_036.text: She did not know whether those old accounts survived in the closed office. Her own grandmother's receipt was at home because people kept things after the work that explained them changed. Du wrote sleeping jars on the wrapper, then asked permission to quote the term publicly. She allowed it. The nephew left briefly to bring the well keeper's sister, whose family had used the outer court for garden sorting. She came by the firm path in her yellow cloth and remained outside the entry line. The household mark made her smile in recognition, then narrow her eyes.

desert_p16_037.speaker: narrator
desert_p16_037.text: Her grandmother's storage jars had carried a similar mark. She could identify the family pattern but not say who put it on that weight. She remembered an old account of deposits kept against flood years, each household entitled to a measured return. Du asked whether she possessed any family papers. She did, at home, and offered to show a public receipt after the day's garden work. The sister pointed to the outer shade where she sorted bulbs. She said the wall was useful long after the office ceased paying for it.

desert_p16_038.speaker: narrator
desert_p16_038.text: Gao asked whether the households maintained any part of the court. They cleared fallen brush and avoided the broken corner, the woman said, but had never undertaken structural repairs. The distinction mattered. Care had continued without turning neighbours into qualified masons. The visiting mason thanked her for keeping children off the unstable rubble. She said they were clever children and needed reminding weekly. He replied that clever adults needed it more often. Du looked down at the very rubble he had wanted to stand on for a better view.

desert_p16_039.speaker: narrator
desert_p16_039.text: The conservator explained that the room's objects would remain in place unless immediate condition and the permitted custody plan required a supported transfer. The older woman asked whether outsiders often found old work and treated it as ownerless. Nobody answered comfortably. Gao said the enquiry would list the community's living accounts beside the official inventory. The woman nodded, then pointed to a rubbed patch near the shutter where children had leaned their shoulders over the years. The room had been closed, but the wall had not ceased belonging to the village's daily path.

desert_p16_040.speaker: narrator
desert_p16_040.text: She returned to the garden before the visitors could turn her into another source kept all day beside a table. Bao asked the older woman how far the garden strip lay beyond the footbridge. The woman measured it by a song she sang while carrying bulbs. Bao smiled, then obtained a practical walking interval from the nephew. The song was not discarded; Yue asked the woman to sing its first line when they were away from the paper. She did so in the court, a low tune about onions keeping secrets beneath their skins. Du looked delighted by the metaphor.

desert_p16_041.speaker: narrator
desert_p16_041.text: The singer told him it was a washing song, not a message from the ancient office. Bao laughed until she had to set her bag down. Even Du managed to enjoy being corrected that way. Bao came to the outer court when the first entry was complete. She checked the shade and the short route back to camp, then asked the mason about any dust exposure the indoor work created. The conservator kept the handling minimal and used plain protective cloth appropriate to the task.

desert_p16_042.speaker: narrator
desert_p16_042.text: Yue's throat felt dry, not ill; she drank from her assigned daily vessel and waited outside while the room settled. Bao refused Du's suggestion that old dust could be distinguished by its smell. He had meant it romantically. She informed him that romance did not improve lungs. The nephew laughed, and Du accepted the correction with an exaggerated little bow. Yue walked to the upper shoulder with Bao to fetch a clean cloth from the kit. The municipal driver was mending a strap with his own checked awl. He asked whether old papers could really affect a present road.

desert_p16_043.speaker: narrator
desert_p16_043.text: Bao said some could show old drainage works, and some might explain why households cared about them. Neither was a substitute for the current assessment. The driver nodded and held up the strap repair for Yue to inspect. She knew less about it than he did and said so. He explained the stitch's purpose. It was pleasant to be taught something that would not demand a public answer by afternoon. Gao stepped away to compare the channel's current level with the morning reading. It had risen slightly, still below the lower splash boundary but closer than the household observer liked.

desert_p16_044.speaker: narrator
desert_p16_044.text: The northern clouds had thickened. The direct quarry branch was only part of the receiving flow; the older valley collected runoff from a larger catchment beyond the visible hills. A local adjustment upstream could reduce one input without arresting every arriving stream. She added that fact to the urgent account. The old municipal trace showed the catchment faintly under a later road line. She did not discover a new river; she stopped letting a convenient small map conceal its actual size. At the channel observation point, a foamy twig caught against the lower lip and spun in place.

desert_p16_045.speaker: narrator
desert_p16_045.text: Gao timed the level check from the same stable mark used that morning. The slight rise was real within the reading's ordinary limits; she did not inflate it into a flood because the clouds made a flood easy to imagine. The household observer had already moved a child's play board away from the lower path. The child objected until the observer offered a safer wall to draw on. Their small bargain continued beside Gao's work. Attention could look like a measurement, or like finding a child another piece of stone before the water reached the first.

desert_p16_046.speaker: gao_ru
desert_p16_046.text: The quarry gate can alter the diverted contribution. It cannot switch off rain across those hills, and water already in the channel will not vanish because a foreman closes a board. We need both kinds of information in the warning. The households should keep the lower crossing observed, and our departure route must be checked again if the level changes. Du, your old inventory may contain useful grades. If we can read them safely, good. But the present level has a job to do today, before the oldest page agrees to answer.

desert_p16_047.speaker: gao_ru
desert_p16_047.text: I will not make the valley wait for my satisfaction with its history.

desert_p16_048.speaker: narrator
desert_p16_048.text: Gao's warning about the larger catchment annoyed the younger household representative. He had hoped the quarry gate would become a simple person to blame or bargain with. She spread the municipal trace and showed him the tributary lines. He followed them with his finger, stopping where the paper ended. There was country beyond that edge too. The representative asked whether a wider map existed. Du said one did, though it was older and less detailed. He would request it from town when they returned. The man sighed, then sent another observer toward the upper runnel.

desert_p16_049.speaker: narrator
desert_p16_049.text: He could not have a simple river, but he could learn more of the one he had. Tuo received the level note at the upper turn and asked Gao to draw the high-water reference in a darker line. Her old winter memory put flood silt higher on the outer wall than the current path sketch. The nephew remembered a similar stain from the last big storm but had never connected it to the old code. Gao compared both accounts with the visible stain from a safe position.

desert_p16_050.speaker: narrator
desert_p16_050.text: Its age remained uncertain, but its height suggested the valley had known larger water. The mason wanted the carts kept ready and the lighter return route rechecked early. They had enough warning to prepare, without enough evidence to know precisely when preparation would be needed. Tuo described the winter silt stain as a height she had seen beneath frost, not a flood she had watched arrive. Gao made that limit visible beside the mark. Tuo approved and asked whether the new map would include the outer household path by name. Du said he needed the current name from its users.

desert_p16_051.speaker: narrator
desert_p16_051.text: The nephew called it the Onion String because children could walk it linked hand to hand. Tuo said that was a good name for a route that ought not carry carts. The nephew agreed and insisted that the printed label include footpath. He had seen names become invitations when printers wanted a road to look generous. At midday the party ate beneath the sound outer wall, away from the unsupported corner. The visiting mason preferred to inspect his food as little as possible. He had spent the morning inspecting everything else.

desert_p16_052.speaker: narrator
desert_p16_052.text: The conservator shared the spice pinch, now nearly exhausted, and Du produced one onion-skin flower for her umbrella handle. She asked what professional standard it improved. He said visibility. She tied it to the handle and declared the umbrella measurable at last. Yue laughed with a mouth full of flatbread and had to turn aside until she could swallow. The relay court acquired an hour of ordinary company before it became old evidence again. At lunch the conservator asked Yue what she had done before the kiln.

desert_p16_053.speaker: narrator
desert_p16_053.text: Yue gave a short account of several places and left the parts that needed a longer friendship for another day. The woman accepted the boundaries as naturally as she accepted a page's unhandled edge. She talked about her own reading-house apprenticeship instead, about repairing wrappers before anybody trusted her with contents. Du said map apprentices should spend a month doing that. Gao suggested he could arrange it for his current apprentice, on paid working time. He looked thoughtful. Yue had learned to notice when a new proposal acquired the words paid time.

desert_p16_054.speaker: narrator
desert_p16_054.text: They made it less likely to survive only as a kindly speech. The nephew returned with news that the market wagon had left carrying the urgent message. Its driver knew the named foreman and would seek him at the quarry receiving yard, not merely leave the paper beneath a closed office shutter. There could still be no immediate answer at the relay. Gao gave the household representatives the current level change and catchment account on their own copy. They chose an additional observer for the lower gardens and began moving loose tools off the low path.

desert_p16_055.speaker: narrator
desert_p16_055.text: The visitors did not direct the households into a panic. People had onions to harvest and channels to watch, and wanted both tasks described without condescension. The market message's departure made Du restless in a different way. Until then the historical work had felt like the party's principal contribution. Now a current note was travelling toward people who might change an actual gate before his fragment was legible. He tried to be pleased and did not quite succeed. The conservator saw his face and asked whether he wanted a task.

desert_p16_056.speaker: narrator
desert_p16_056.text: She had him label the modern support sleeves, one by one, with the site and date. By the sixth sleeve his impatience had turned into careful handwriting. Old pride could be redirected through ordinary work if a person was willing to remain in the room while it happened. After the meal the conservator lifted only the loose modern-sized fragment already resting outside the failed box, using a thin support and the mason-cleared near strip. The fragment lay flat enough to be supported without bending.

desert_p16_057.speaker: narrator
desert_p16_057.text: She placed it in a clean temporary sleeve, recorded its position and condition, and kept it in the site's handling box under the district custody terms. No private pocket received it. Its visible text listed water allotments for work crews by season. Several figures differed from the cleaner printed summary Du knew. He leaned close enough to make her ask him to breathe away from the page. He backed up, smiling despite himself. The supported fragment had a torn edge like small teeth.

desert_p16_058.speaker: narrator
desert_p16_058.text: The conservator showed Yue where fibre continuity remained strong enough to carry it and where a slightest fold would break text. Yue held the clean modern board while the woman made the transfer. The page seemed impossibly light compared with the care around it. Du read the first visible season aloud, then stopped himself before guessing the next. The nephew repeated the temporary-closure mark's meaning. Outside, the swallow returned to its nest with another bead of mud. The room contained two kinds of painstaking construction, one old enough to be failing and one still wet on a bird's beak.

desert_p16_059.speaker: narrator
desert_p16_059.text: The differences did not prove theft. One heading distinguished raw channel work water from the treated household draw, while the printed summary had combined the headings into source provision. Another line marked a temporary closure, apparently reflected later as a reduction in ordinary allotment. Du had seen those words in the transfer correspondence without their table. He began to understand how an office abstraction could turn a seasonal household arrangement into a simple freight station. The conservator let him read what was visible but stopped him from completing damaged numbers from memory.

desert_p16_060.speaker: narrator
desert_p16_060.text: Yue copied the gaps just as carefully as the intact figures. The empty spaces were not invitations to make the story tidy. Gao asked Du which printed summary he meant. He fetched his modern copy from the outer court and laid it beside the fragment's transcription, safely away from the original. The merged heading looked harmless until the local closure mark was restored beneath it. The table then described distinct uses in distinct seasons. A clean total had not been false as arithmetic; it had been poor as an instruction for who could draw what.

desert_p16_061.speaker: narrator
desert_p16_061.text: The nephew understood immediately because the well court still separated household reserve from daily draw. Du took longer, troubled by how elegant the merged line had looked. He crossed it out in his working copy with a stroke almost angry enough to tear the paper.

desert_p16_062.speaker: du_she
desert_p16_062.text: I thought the old household deposits ended when the relay office closed. The summary called them absorbed into district provision. This fragment says some remained separately credited until the transfer. That does not establish anybody's present entitlement by itself. We need the transfer account and living claims. But it means my assumption was not the only possible reading, and I printed it as if it were. The full table may still be in the box. I want that table more than I wanted it yesterday.

desert_p16_063.speaker: du_she
desert_p16_063.text: I also know wanting it is the worst reason to ask you to lift a lid before you are ready.

desert_p16_064.speaker: narrator
desert_p16_064.text: The conservator asked him to put the pen down before he damaged his own evidence. He did, then rubbed his eyes with empty fingers. He had wanted the records to reveal somebody else's failure, even while promising to correct his own. The fragment was proving inconveniently mixed: useful office work, careless summaries, local contributions, interruptions from weather and transfer. No single villain would make the route easier to understand. Yue told him the clean wrapper could hold all those headings. He looked at the wrapper and laughed weakly.

desert_p16_065.speaker: narrator
desert_p16_065.text: She had become very good at giving him more space when he had hoped for fewer things to say. Yue asked what would happen if the full table had decayed. Du looked at the failed box and took a long time to answer. Then he said the fragment would remain evidence of its own limited statements, and the office would have to state what it could not recover. His disappointment was visible. It made the answer more convincing.

desert_p16_066.speaker: narrator
desert_p16_066.text: The conservator prepared a shallow support arrangement for the box's near edge, but the brittle lid needed a longer condition review than the remaining afternoon could fairly supply. She stopped rather than begin a task that dusk might force her to hurry. Du did not object. He packed the copied fragment with hands that shook slightly from fatigue. The conservator's decision to stop handling for the afternoon produced a quiet protest from no one and a loud sigh from Du. She asked whether he believed tomorrow would contain no old pages. He said tomorrow might contain weather.

desert_p16_067.speaker: narrator
desert_p16_067.text: She agreed, which was why the condition records, fragment copy and custody notes had to be secured before evening. He helped secure them. The mason confirmed that the cleared near strip remained as assessed; nothing in that confirmation made the damaged rear corner available. Gao drew the closed handling arrangement and the exact place from which it could be resumed. On the return to camp, the nephew showed Yue a notch in the outer wall where a branch had rubbed for years. The notch looked like writing until one stood close enough to see its rough grain.

desert_p16_068.speaker: narrator
desert_p16_068.text: A childhood rumour had called it the relay's secret password. The nephew had believed it until he cut back the branch and watched the mark stop growing. Yue liked the explanation. A place could hold genuine lost information without every scratch hiding a code. She drew the notch and the absent branch, planning to tell the shoemaker's girl someday. The girl would probably ask why nobody had sharpened a pencil on it instead. The notch made by the missing branch had collected pale dust along one side.

desert_p16_069.speaker: narrator
desert_p16_069.text: Yue could see how it resembled a letter at a distance and a scrape up close. The nephew said he had been disappointed when the branch explained it. Then he had used the freed corner to store the hoe out of rain. That had proved more useful than a password. Yue asked whether he wanted to leave the notch on the site sketch. He said yes, as a recognizable mark, provided no publisher sold it as a secret. Du, overhearing, held up both hands. His reputation had become a shared village joke faster than he could issue a correction.

desert_p16_070.speaker: narrator
desert_p16_070.text: Tuo was waiting at the upper turn with a folded local receipt the older sister had delivered. The sister's grandmother had paid a household contribution toward the covered well reserve. The receipt bore a similar rough mark and a date compatible with the fragment's operating season. Similarity and dates made a comparison worth recording, not a present title created by resemblance. Gao copied the receipt with the owner's permission and returned it before dinner. Tuo watched Du read. She said he looked as if he had found an embarrassing relative in a locked room.

desert_p16_071.speaker: narrator
desert_p16_071.text: He replied that it might be his entire profession. She handed him ginger broth before he could improve the joke. The receipt Tuo brought was wrapped in a piece of yellowed household cloth. It listed a contribution and a receiving season, with the rough crossed-stem mark beside a clerk's formal entry. Du identified the clerk's notation from another record, then carefully limited the identification to style rather than the unknown person's name. The grandmother's contribution was real on the receipt, but its later settlement remained in the transfer sequence they had not recovered. The older sister understood this.

desert_p16_072.speaker: narrator
desert_p16_072.text: She had brought the paper because the family had work in the well's history, not because she expected a stranger to declare the entire source hers before supper. The older sister's niece had avoided the provoking stone lift that day, using lighter tasks with the young worker instead. Bao checked that the shoulder pain had not increased. The garden wall still needed a final cap; they planned to finish it the following morning if the footbridge observer and weather allowed. The household representatives knew the plan.

desert_p16_073.speaker: narrator
desert_p16_073.text: At that evening's level, the local foot line remained as assessed and the three workers returned safely again. Gao did not give them a surveyor's guarantee for dawn. The observer would inspect before anyone crossed. The valley's everyday work continued, but now the continuing had a little more attention inside it. The young garden worker asked the municipal driver whether he would carry a course enquiry to the town school. The driver agreed to carry the written enquiry and the return-address instruction, not to promise admission.

desert_p16_074.speaker: narrator
desert_p16_074.text: The worker used another scrap from Yue's purchased bundle and wrote slowly, consulting his older companion about one character. His niece companion teased him for making a formal letter to a metal room. He said a metal room that accepted him would deserve formality. Bao smiled at the determination, then asked both younger workers to keep the next day's wall tasks light. Their ambition could survive one unlifted stone. The crew used one hundred and nineteen litres that day, leaving nine hundred and thirty-eight, four hundred and sixty-nine in each tank. The two protected hundred-litre compartments remained intact.

desert_p16_075.speaker: narrator
desert_p16_075.text: Fuel stood at twenty-eight kilograms after another four used for meals and ordinary camp preparation. The visible well remained within its keeper's current routine, with no caravan draw taken or added. Bao noted the changed channel level as a reason for repeated source observation, not a diagnosis. Yue finished the common account while Du worked on the readable fragment. The two tasks sat beside each other under the same lamp, one certain in its count, the other honest about the numbers it could not yet see.

desert_p16_076.speaker: narrator
desert_p16_076.text: The fuel count was made by weight rather than by judging how large the bags looked after settling. The second driver held the yard-issued spring scale while Gao recorded the remaining twenty-eight kilograms. Du asked whether a bag of onions should be included under combustible enthusiasm. The cook would have been proud of the question and offended by the lentils. Yue entered the fuel correctly and let the joke go unrecorded. The nine travellers had become familiar enough to be tired together without taking every tired look as dislike.

desert_p16_077.speaker: narrator
desert_p16_077.text: Bao sent Tuo to raise her foot, and the guide obeyed while continuing to complain about Du's onion metaphor. After dark, a deeper note came from the relay's high slit when the north wind reached it. The nephew had told them to expect a whistle; this sounded more like breath blown over a bottle. Yue listened without imagining a creature inside. The sound changed as the wind changed and stopped when the gust passed. Du looked toward the dark court and said the room had waited a long time for readers.

desert_p16_078.speaker: narrator
desert_p16_078.text: The conservator replied that rooms did not wait, but pages sometimes outlasted the people who meant to read them. She closed her box. Beyond the valley, the northern clouds hid the stars. Morning would bring light across the floor, if the water allowed them to remain. The conservator slept with the supported fragment in the dry custody box beside her place, secured according to the district plan and inventoried on the common sheet. Du's modern transcription rested in his own folder. The original letter remained separately sleeved.

desert_p16_079.speaker: narrator
desert_p16_079.text: Those different kinds of paper would not merge merely because they shared a night. Yue checked the common lamp before the last watch and lowered its wick. The room's wind note sounded once from across the shoulder, low and brief. Beyond it, water moved through the spill throat in the dark. Tomorrow light might make the old floor easier to read; it would make the current channel easier to read as well.
